title: Normality over a DVR from normal generic and reduced special fibres
statement: Let $R$ be a discrete valuation ring [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring] with uniformizer $\pi$, fraction field $L$, and residue field $k=R/\pi R$. Let $T$ be a finitely generated commutative $R$-algebra, flat as an $R$-module [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. Suppose $T_L=T\otimes_R L=T[1/\pi]$ is a normal ring [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring] and $T/\pi T$ is reduced, meaning it has no nonzero nilpotent elements. Then $T$ is a normal ring. Moreover, under the injective localization map $T\to T_L$, every element of $T_L$ satisfying a monic polynomial over $T$ belongs to $T$. No normality of the special fibre is assumed. The zero algebra and an empty special fibre are allowed.

source.place: WANTED locally; read https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0405381, Appendix Remark A.3, printed p.27, paragraph on Serre criteria: a finite-type flat scheme over a normal Noetherian domain is normal when its generic fibre is normal and its other fibres are reduced. The final integral-closure formulation is the affine normal-ring characterization.

proof.text: Put $t=\pi\cdot1_T$ and $B=T[1/t]=T_L$. Multiplication by $\pi$ on $R$ is injective since $R$ is a domain and $\pi\ne0$. Tensor this injective $R$-linear map with the flat module $T$. Under $R\otimes_RT\simeq T$, the resulting map is multiplication by $t$, hence is injective by the definition of flatness. Every power of $t$ is therefore a nonzerodivisor, and the localization zero criterion shows that $T\to B$ is injective.

source.place: Tag 055J, lemma-connected-flat-over-dvr, proof: uniformizer nonzerodivisor; the tensor argument is written out here.

proof.text: First prove the asserted integral-closure clause directly. For $z\in B$ integral over $T$, choose a representation $z=a/t^n$ with $n\ge0$ minimal. If $n>0$, substitute this expression into a monic equation $z^d+\sum_{i=0}^{d-1}c_i z^i=0$ with $d\ge1$ and multiply by $t^{nd}$. Injectivity from step 1 gives $a^d+\sum_{i=0}^{d-1}c_i a^i t^{n(d-i)}=0$ in $T$. Modulo $tT$ this says $\overline a^d=0$. Reducedness of $T/tT$ implies $a=tb$ for some $b\in T$, so $z=b/t^{n-1}$, contradicting minimality. Thus $n=0$ and $z\in T$.

source.place: Tag 055J, lemma-connected-flat-over-dvr, proof: least uniformizer denominator; agent extension from the idempotent equation to an arbitrary monic equation.

proof.text: The normal ring $B$ is reduced: its prime localizations are domains by the definition of normality, hence reduced, and the joint injectivity of these localizations implies reducedness of $B$. By the injection $T\hookrightarrow B$, a nilpotent of $T$ is zero. Thus $T$ is reduced.

source.place: Tag 00GV, definition-ring-normal, following paragraph; Tag 00HN, lemma-characterize-zero-local.

proof.text: The DVR $R$ is Noetherian since every ideal is principal. The finite-type algebra theorem implies that $T$ is Noetherian, and the finiteness theorem for minimal primes gives finitely many minimal prime ideals of $T$.

Let $Q(T)$ and $Q(B)$ denote localization at the respective nonzerodivisors. If $s\in T$ is a nonzerodivisor and $(s/1)(a/t^n)=0$ in $B$, the localization zero criterion gives $t^j sa=0$ for some $j$, hence $a=0$. Thus $s/1$ is a nonzerodivisor of $B$, and fractions define $Q(T)\to Q(B)$ by $a/s\mapsto(a/1)/(s/1)$. This map is injective: an image fraction equal to zero has zero numerator in $B$, hence $a=0$ in $T$. For $x\in Q(T)$ integral over $T$, its image is integral over $B$ by mapping its monic equation. Since $B$ is normal, its integral closedness in $Q(B)$ puts this image in $B$. Its monic equation holds already in $B$, since $B\to Q(B)$ is injective by the localization zero criterion. Step 2 then puts that element of $B$ in $T$. The injections into $Q(B)$ show that $x$ itself equals this element of $T$. Therefore $T$ is integrally closed in $Q(T)$.

source.place: Tag 034M, lemma-normal-ring-integrally-closed; fraction maps and their injectivity are checked explicitly using Section 00CM, section-localization.

proof.text: Apply the equivalence between normality and integral closedness in the total fraction ring for a reduced ring with finitely many minimal primes. Its hypotheses are steps 3 and 4, and its integral-closure condition is step 5. It follows that $T$ is normal. Step 2 already proves the additional clause. If $T=0$ all membership assertions are vacuous or equalities in the zero ring and normality is vacuous; the criterion allows the empty product. If the special fibre is empty, $T/tT=0$ is reduced and the same argument applies (indeed $t$ is then a unit).

proof_origin.place: Tag 055J, lemma-connected-flat-over-dvr, least-denominator argument generalized to monic equations, followed by Algebra Tags 034M and 030C. The source assertion is Conrad Appendix Remark A.3 in Prasad--Yu (read online; archival copy WANTED).

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q67-703c4bdff (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole delivery and changed nothing. It has 0 new nodes and its statement is byte-identical to the base statement. In side-live the item is unsplit and there is no repair note, so no other group superseded it. The statement is true: it is the affine DVR case of Serre's criterion in Conrad's Remark A.3. Edge cases: T=0 holds, and an empty special fibre means pi is a unit, so it holds. Without reducedness it fails: in R[x]/(x^2-pi^2), x/pi is integral over T but not in T. Without flatness it fails: in R[x]/(pi x), T->T_L is not injective. Steps checked one by one: (1) pi is a nonzerodivisor on T by flatness and the zero criterion, so T->T[1/t] is injective. (2) The least-denominator argument generalizes the idempotent case in the proof of Stacks 055J (more-morphisms lemma-connected-flat-over-dvr) to any monic equation: multiplying by t^{nd} makes every term except a^d divisible by t, so a^d is in tT, reducedness gives a=tb, and minimality of n fails; this proves the integral-closure clause. (3) Lemma 00HN gives B reduced, hence T reduced. (4) Lemmas 00FN and 00FR give T Noetherian with finitely many minimal primes. (5) Q(T)->Q(B) is well defined and injective (written out); Lemma 034M for B and then step 2 put an integral x into T. (6) Lemma 030C, implication (2)=>(1), gives normality. I read the cited statements and the Stacks source for 034M, 030C and 055J. The duplicate search with rg -L over dag/nodes found no node stating the same thing or generalizing it. The declared tool_uses 034M and 030C (unit sk-thm-p1) are generic commutative algebra and replace no step of the unit route; I accept them. There is no SGA citation.
